proposals.quote: Resorts World has offered a community benefits package consisting of an annual commitment, for the duration of the license term, of the lesser of 2 percent of incremental gross gaming revenue above 2025 levels, or $25 million per year, for a workforce housing fund. Resorts World has partnered with Cirrus Workforce Housing Advisors on this initiative, but the substance is vague, with the promised investments in workforce housing to begin “in the immediate term.”

RWNYC recently formed a joint venture with Cirrus Workforce Housing to contribute up to $25 million each year, over the term of the License, to help fund the construction of up to 50,000 units of workforce housing throughout New York City.

Resorts World's Workforce Housing Initiative, funded through the Cirrus Workforce Housing Fund, is a landmark partnership with organized labor to deliver tens of thousands of new homes for working families across New York City.
Approximately 3,000 units of union-built and labor-financed workforce housing would also be created.

Queens, NY Cirrus WFHA Funding LLC, an affiliate of Cirrus Real Estate Partners acting in partnership with Resorts World New York City, has acquired the 1.8-acre development site and parking garage at 92-30 165th St. in Jamaica for $46.125 million in a transaction brokered by RIPCO Real Estate. The property offers more than 600,000 buildable s/f and represents the first acquisition under the partners’ workforce housing initiative.

The transaction also represents the largest development site sale completed in Jamaica since the adoption of the Jamaica Neighborhood Plan, underscoring the neighborhood’s emergence as one of New York City’s most active development markets.
The acquisition of this property demonstrates our commitment to transforming well-located sites into high-quality workforce housing that creates lasting value for communities,

As the first project under our workforce housing initiative with Resorts World, this development will set the tone for what we hope to achieve across New York City: creating attainable housing in transit-oriented locations while supporting long-term neighborhood growth and economic opportunity.
The acquisition of 92-30 165th St. is the first transaction completed under that initiative.
